t: This bronze memorial on Portland Place, opposite BBC Broadcasting House, shows Quintin Hogg with two boys, standing on a plinth of Portland stone. It was designed by the sculptor George Frampton and put up in 1906. Hogg was a merchant and philanthropist, remembered as the benefactor of the Regent Street Polytechnic, now the University of Westminster. The memorial also honours his wife Alice, and members of the Polytechnic who were killed in the two world wars. Frampton is also known for the Edith Cavell Memorial and the Peter Pan statue in Kensington Gardens.
